**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Base Terms sit at the **preferred** position for MINCOMMIT:

- **No commitment mechanic exists.** Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay", "purchase" and "volume" surface nothing relevant. § 4.1 charges only for ordered Services on a one-time, installment, recurring or usage basis.
- **§ 11.5 Capacity Planning is not a volume commitment.** It allocates forecasting responsibility to Customer and lets Customer request capacity changes "as determined by Customer" — a discretion in our favour, so not flagged.
- **Exit right exceeds the fallback.** § 3.4 gives Customer convenience termination of the Agreement or any single Service Option Attachment at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice; § 3.3 bars IBM from recovering early termination charges where IBM has breached.

Two diligence notes recorded in the rationale rather than flagged as deviations, since both live outside the text under review:

1. § 3.4(b) conditions the convenience exit on "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments."
2. § 3.5 preserves charges under non-terminated Service Option Attachments.

Any committed spend, minimum volume, or penalty-style termination-charge formula would have to appear in those attachments or Order Forms. Worth re-running this rule against the commercial schedules when issued — if a shortfall penalty shows up there, the redline guidance (narrow to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up instead of penalty) would apply at that point.
